claims.source: Inactivation of the eIF2 complex leads to a shutdown of global protein synthesis but also the induction of preferential translation of transcripts notably the mRNAs of transcription factors, Activating Transcription Factor 4 (ATF4) and C/EBP homologous protein (CHOP, encoded by Ddit3), and other factors with both pro-survival and pro-death functions which aid cell adaption and recovery (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) (Harding et al., 2000).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: CHOP is encoded by Ddit3.
claims.source: Inactivation of the eIF2 complex leads to a shutdown of global protein synthesis but also the induction of preferential translation of transcripts notably the mRNAs of transcription factors, Activating Transcription Factor 4 (ATF4) and C/EBP homologous protein (CHOP, encoded by Ddit3), and other factors with both pro-survival and pro-death functions which aid cell adaption and recovery (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) (Harding et al., 2000).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge.

claims.claim: eIF2α phosphorylation is transient and can be reversed by PPP1R15A (GADD34) or CReP1.
claims.source: eIF2α phosphorylation is transient and can be reversed by PPP1R15A (GADD34) or CReP1, the regulatory subunit of eIF2α phosphatases, acting in a negative feedback loop that allows protein synthesis to restart (Harding et al., 2009; Novoa et al., 2001).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: PPP1R15A and CReP1 act in a negative feedback loop that allows protein synthesis to restart.
claims.source: eIF2α phosphorylation is transient and can be reversed by PPP1R15A (GADD34) or CReP1, the regulatory subunit of eIF2α phosphatases, acting in a negative feedback loop that allows protein synthesis to restart (Harding et al., 2009; Novoa et al., 2001).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: When stress is intense or prolonged, cells fail to adapt and apoptosis is triggered.
claims.source: When the stress is intense or prolonged, cells fail to adapt, and apoptosis is triggered.
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claims.claim: The duration and level of eIF2α phosphorylation, as well as ATF4 regulation, determine the balance between cell survival and cell death.
claims.source: It is likely that the duration and level of eIF2α phosphorylation, as well as ATF4 regulation, determine the balance between cell survival and cell death.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the established knowledge presented.

claims.claim: There are more than 400 human genetic skeletal disorders caused by disrupted cartilage and bone development and growth.
claims.source: There are more than 400 human genetic skeletal disorders caused by disrupted cartilage and bone development and growth, commonly resulting in dwarfism and skeletal deformities (Geister and Camper, 2015).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to published literature.

claims.claim: Many skeletal disorders are caused by mutations in genes for extracellular matrix (ECM) proteins.
claims.source: Many of these disorders are caused by mutations in genes for extracellular matrix (ECM) proteins (Geister and Camper, 2015; Bonafe et al., 2015; Briggs and Chapman, 2002; Warman et al., 1993)
claims.evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claims.claim: Some mutations in ECM protein genes cause inappropriate folding, processing or export, leading to retention in the ER.
claims.source: and some mutations cause inappropriate folding, processing or export, leading to retention in the ER, affecting the secretory and stress response pathways (Wilson et al., 2005; Tsang et al., 2007; Tsang et al., 2010; Posey et al., 2012; PirogPiróg-Garcia et al., 2007; Hartley et al., 2013; Cameron et al., 2011; Boot-Handford and Briggs, 2010; Arnold and Fertala, 2013).
claims.evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claims.claim: Accumulation of misfolded proteins in the ER can overwhelm the protein quality control mechanism, causing proteotoxicity, cell cycle arrest and cell death.
claims.source: Accumulation of misfolded proteins in the ER can overwhelm the protein quality control mechanism, causing proteotoxicity, cell cycle arrest and cell death.
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claims.claim: Cells activate the unfolded protein response (UPR) which mediates cell survival by slowing protein translation, promoting proteostasis via the proteasome and activating transcription factors that upregulate the production of protein chaperones.
claims.source: Cells activate the unfolded protein response (UPR), which mediates cell survival by slowing protein translation, promoting proteostasis via the proteasome and activating transcription factors that upregulate the production of protein chaperones (reviewed in [Hotamisligil and Davis, 2016; Horiuchi et al., 2016]).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to review articles.

claims.claim: The UPR employs three arms of sensors in the ER: PERK, IRE1α, and the ATF6 family.
claims.source: The UPR employs three arms of sensors in the ER to mediate cell adaptation and survival under ER stress: the key component of the ISR, PERK, inositol-regulated enzyme 1α (IRE1α), and the activating transcription factor 6 (ATF6) family (Hotamisligil and Davis, 2016; Horiuchi et al., 2016; Walter and Ron, 2011).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: Upon ER stress, the PERK-p-eIF2α signaling modulates cell adaptation via translational control.
claims.source: Upon ER stress, the PERK-p-eIF2α signaling modulates the cell adaptation via translational control.
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claims.claim: ATF6 family factors move from the ER to the Golgi, are processed by S1 and S2 proteases, and translocate to the nucleus to activate ER quality control genes such as Hspa5 and Xbp1.
claims.source: ATF6 family factors move from the ER to the Golgi, are processed by S1 and S2 proteases, and translocate to the nucleus to activate ER quality control genes such as Hspa5 (encodes BiP) and Xbp1 (X-box binding protein 1).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claims.claim: IRE1α has kinase and endoribonuclease (RNase) activities.
claims.source: IRE1α has kinase and endoribonuclease (RNase) activities.
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claims.claim: IRE1α catalyzes the splicing of Xbp1 mRNA, generating the UPR transcription factor XBP1S.
claims.source: It catalyzes the splicing of Xbp1 mRNA, generating the UPR transcription factor XBP1S that upregulates genes encoding chaperones and proteins involved in ER-associated protein degradation (ERAD).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claims.claim: XBP1S upregulates genes encoding chaperones and proteins involved in ER-associated protein degradation (ERAD).
claims.source: It catalyzes the splicing of Xbp1 mRNA, generating the UPR transcription factor XBP1S that upregulates genes encoding chaperones and proteins involved in ER-associated protein degradation (ERAD).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claims.claim: In the MCDS transgenic mouse model (13del), misfolded mutant collagen X induces ER stress.
claims.source: In an MCDS transgenic mouse model (13del), carrying a 13 bp deletion in Col10a1 equivalent to the human mutation, misfolded mutant collagen X induces ER stress suggesting the primary role of ER stress in MCDS pathogenesis (Tsang et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claims.claim: In 13del mice, chondrocyte differentiation is reversed to a more juvenile state characterized by re-expression of prehypertrophic chondrocyte markers.
claims.source: Although the chondrocytes survive, their differentiation is reversed by an unknown mechanism to a more juvenile state characterized by the re-expression of prehypertrophic chondrocyte markers (Ppr, Sox9 and Col2a1), disrupting endochondral ossification, and skeletal dysplasia ensues.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from previous work on the 13del model.

claims.claim: Expression of an exogenous misfolded protein in HCs can induce an MCDS-like phenotype.
claims.source: The causative role of ER stress in MCDS is further supported by studies showing that expression of an exogenous misfolded protein in HCs can induce an MCDS-like phenotype (Rajpar et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to published work.

claims.claim: Skeletal defects caused by mutations that induce stress or inactivate critical transducers of the stress response in humans and mouse models implicate components of ER stress-induced UPR pathways in chondrocyte and osteoblast differentiation.
claims.source: It is noteworthy that the skeletal defects caused by mutations that induce stress or inactivate critical transducers of the stress response in humans (Julier and Nicolino, 2010) and mouse models (Tsang et al., 2007; Cameron et al., 2011; Horiuchi et al., 2016; Rajpar et al., 2009; Julier and Nicolino, 2010; Nundlall et al., 2010; Cameron et al., 2015a2015; Cameron et al., 2015b) strongly implicate components of ER stress-induced UPR pathways involved in chondrocyte and osteoblast differentiation (Tsang et al., 2010; Horiuchi et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claims.claim: Expression of misfolded cartilage oligomeric matrix protein (COMP) in proliferating and hypertrophic chondrocytes results in chondrocyte disorganization and causes Pseudoachondroplasia (PSACH).
claims.source: Expression of misfolded cartilage oligomeric matrix protein (COMP) in proliferating and hypertrophic chondrocytes results in chondrocyte disorganization and causes Pseudoachondroplasia (PSACH), suggesting triggering the UPR may underlie many chondrodysplasias where mutations cause accumulation of misfolded proteins (Posey et al., 2012; Piróg et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claims.claim: Bbf2h7 null mutants show severe chondrocyte abnormality due to proliferation and differentiation defects.
claims.source: Another example that links ER stress signaling to chondrocyte differentiation is illustrated by studies on BBF2H7, an ER stress transducer. Bbf2h7 null mutants show severe chondrocyte abnormality due to proliferation and differentiation defects, indicating its essential role for chondrogenesis (Saito et al., 2009; Saito et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claims.claim: BBF2H7 suppresses chondrocyte hypertrophy by direct regulation of IHH signaling and the IHH-PTHrP pathway.
claims.source: Furthermore, BBF2H7 has been shown to suppress chondrocyte hypertrophy by direct regulation of IHH signaling and the IHH-PTHrP pathway (Saito et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to published literature.

claims.claim: Pharmacological stimulation of intracellular proteolysis of mutant collagen X in an MCDS mouse model reduces the level of ER stress and partially ameliorates the dwarfism phenotype.
claims.source: Pharmacological stimulation of intracellular proteolysis of mutant collagen X in another MCDS mouse model reduces the level of ER stress, partially ameliorating the dwarfism phenotype (Mullan et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to published literature.

claims.claim: Stimulating degradation of misfolded protein alone is not sufficient to address the impact of ER stress on aberrant cell differentiation in MCDS.
claims.source: However, the rescue of the chondrocyte differentiation defect, expansion of the hypertrophic zone and bone growth was incomplete, suggesting stimulating degradation of misfolded protein alone is not sufficient to address the impact of the ER stress on aberrant cell differentiation.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the incomplete rescue observed in the cited study.

claims.claim: The mammalian growth plate comprises four major sub-populations of chondrocytes: resting, proliferating (PC), prehypertrophic (pHC) and hypertrophic chondrocytes (HC).
claims.source: The mammalian growth plate comprises four major sub-populations of chondrocytes: resting, proliferating (PC), prehypertrophic (pHC) and hypertrophic chondrocytes (HC).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claims.claim: Chondrocytes in the growth plate have distinct morphologies and gene expression profiles governed by a precisely tuned gene regulatory network.
claims.source: These chondrocytes have distinct morphologies and gene expression profiles governed by a precisely tuned gene regulatory network (Hojo et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claims.claim: Proximal tibial growth plates from 10-day-old WT and 13del mice were fractionated into sub-populations representing proliferating (PZ), prehypertrophic (pHZ) and hypertrophic chondrocytes (HZ).
claims.source: To investigate the effect of ER stress on the transcriptome of HCs, the proximal tibial growth plates from 10-day-old WT and 13del mice were fractionated into sub-populations representing proliferating (PZ), prehypertrophic (pHZ) and hypertrophic chondrocytes (HZ) (Figure 1A; Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is a methodological description supported by Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: The wild-type HZ was fractionated into upper and lower zones (UHZ and LHZ) to capture early onset and late phases of hypertrophy.
claims.source: The wild-type HZ was fractionated into upper and lower zones (UHZ and LHZ) to capture early onset and late phases of hypertrophy.
claims.evidence: This is a methodological description.

claims.claim: The 13del HZ was fractionated into three zones: upper (UHZ), middle (MHZ), and lower (LHZ).
claims.source: The 13del HZ was fractionated into three zones: upper (UHZ) corresponding to the early phase of UPR activation, middle (MHZ) where HC adaptation would be initiated, and lower (LHZ) where HC should fully adapt.
claims.evidence: This is a methodological description.

claims.claim: K-means clustering categorized gene expression patterns across different zones in wild-type and 13del growth plates into four clusters.
claims.source: We used k-means clustering (see Materials and methods) to categorize the gene expression patterns across different zones in wild-type and 13del growth plates into four clusters (Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: This is a methodological description and analysis result.

claims.claim: Cluster I contains 453 genes that increased expression from PHZ to lower HZ specifically in 13del HC.
claims.source: Genes (453) in Cluster I increased expression from PHZ to lower HZ specifically in 13del HC (Figure 1B and C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Figure 1B and C showing the clustering analysis.

claims.claim: Cluster I genes are mainly involved in protein processing in the ER and the UPR.
claims.source: Ontological analyses show these differentially expressed genes are mainly involved in protein processing in the ER and the UPR (Figure 1D and E, Supplementary file 2 and 3).
claims.evidence: This is supported by ontological analyses shown in Figure 1D and E.

claims.claim: Cluster II contains 659 genes and Cluster III contains 314 genes that showed highest expression in wild-type PZ and pHZ followed by progressive downregulation from pHZ to LHZ but were upregulated in 13del LHZ.
claims.source: Genes in Clusters II (659) and III (314) showed highest expression in wild-type PZ and pHZ followed by progressive downregulation from pHZ to LHZ but were upregulated in 13del LHZ, reflecting UPR-induced changes in HC differentiation (Figure 1B and C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Figure 1B and C showing the clustering analysis.

claims.claim: Cluster II and III genes include Sox9, Ppr, and Ihh.
claims.source: These genes included Sox9, Ppr, and Ihh, consistent with our previous report of re-expression of pre-hypertrophic markers (Tsang et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This is supported by the clustering analysis and previous work.

claims.claim: Cluster IV contains 680 genes showing increasing expression from pHZ to LHZ in wild-type and can be defined as 'hypertrophy characteristic' genes.
claims.source: Cluster IV genes (680) showed increasing expression from pHZ to LHZ in wild-type and can be defined as 'hypertrophy characteristic' genes.
claims.evidence: This is supported by the clustering analysis.

claims.claim: Cluster IV genes were down-regulated in 13del LHZ.
claims.source: Consistent with a change in the HC de-differentiation state in 13del, these genes were down-regulated in 13del LHZ.
claims.evidence: This is supported by the clustering analysis.

claims.claim: The concomitant down-regulation of Cluster I stress response genes in 13del LHZ is consistent with the alleviation of the stress in the reprogrammed cells and an adapted state.
claims.source: The concomitant down-regulation of Cluster I stress response genes in 13del LHZ is consistent with the alleviation of the stress in the reprogrammed cells and an adapted state.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the clustering data.

claims.claim: 227 genes were commonly changed in the microarray dataset compared with published data from two other MCDS mouse models.
claims.source: We further compared our microarray dataset with the published data (Cameron et al., 2011) from another 2 MCDS mouse models, expressing a Col10a1 p.N617K mutation or an ER stress-inducing form of thyroglobulin (Tgcog) (Cameron et al., 2011). Overall, the gene expression changes detected in all datasets shared some degree of similarity, and 227 genes were commonly changed, showing the activation of ER stress signaling in the MCDS chondrocytes, up-regulation of genes such as Fgf21 and down-regulation of genes such as Ldb3.
claims.evidence: This is supported by comparison with published data.

claims.claim: 473 genes were specifically changed in 13del.
claims.source: Differences were also found, and 473 genes were specifically changed in 13del, such as Apoa4 (up-regulated) and Atp2a1 (down-regulated) (Supplementary file 4).
claims.evidence: This is supported by comparison with published data.

claims.claim: Ontology and pathway analyses of Cluster I found enrichment of genes in the PERK pathway and IRE1-Xbp1S regulated ERAD, but not for ATF6 signaling.
claims.source: By ontology and pathway analyses of Cluster I, we found enrichment of genes in the PERK pathway and IRE1-Xbp1S regulated ERAD, but not for ATF6 signaling (Figure 1D and E; Figure 1—figure supplement 1C; Supplementary file 2 and 3).
claims.evidence: This is supported by ontology and pathway analyses shown in figures.

claims.claim: Activation of PERK signaling in 13del HC was demonstrated by up-regulation of p-eIF2α and its downstream components (Atf4, Atf3, Ddit3, Ero1l and Ppp1r15a).
claims.source: Activation of PERK signaling in 13del HC was demonstrated by up-regulation of p-eIF2α and its downstream components (Atf4, Atf3, Ddit3, Ero1l and Ppp1r15a) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and C) which were validated by in-situ hybridization and immunostaining (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B and C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by microarray data and validated by in-situ hybridization and immunostaining shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: Motif enrichment analysis found that the binding motifs of CHOP and ATF4 were highly enriched in Cluster I, but not those for Xbp1S or ATF6.
claims.source: Using Motif enrichment analysis, we found that the binding motifs of CHOP (encoded by Ddit3) and ATF4 were highly enriched in Cluster I, but not those for Xbp1S or ATF6 (Figure 1F and Supplementary file 5).
claims.evidence: This is supported by motif enrichment analysis shown in Figure 1F.

claims.claim: ATF4 and CHOP ChIP-seq data showed significant over-representation of ATF4 and CHOP binding peaks associated with genes from Cluster I.
claims.source: By interrogating ATF4 and CHOP ChIP-seq data (Han et al., 2013), we found significant over-representation of ATF4 (odds ratio = 2.87, p<0.0001) and CHOP (odds ratio = 4.33, p<0.0001) binding peaks associated with the genes from Cluster I but not for the other clusters (Supplementary file 6).
claims.evidence: This is supported by analysis of published ChIP-seq data.

claims.claim: Cluster I genes are most likely to be directly regulated by UPR-associated transcription factors.
claims.source: Cluster I genes are therefore most likely to be directly regulated by UPR-associated transcription factors.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on motif enrichment and ChIP-seq analyses.

claims.claim: Inactivation of Xbp1 in HCs did not alter the severity of dwarfism in an MCDS mouse model.
claims.source: Together, these data suggest a more prominent contribution of the PERK-p-eIF2 signaling pathway than that of Xbp1S, which is consistent with another MCDS mouse model study that found inactivation of Xbp1 in HCs did not alter the severity of dwarfism (Cameron et al., 2015b).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to published literature.

claims.claim: Overexpression of Xbp1S specifically in HCs did not affect the growth plate.
claims.source: To test this notion, we ectopically expressed Xbp1S in HCs in transgenic mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A). Overexpression of Xbp1S specifically in HCs did not affect the growth plate (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B and C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by data from transgenic mice shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: ATF4 is required for chondrocyte differentiation through direct activation of Ihh.
claims.source: Apart from its role in the stress response, ATF4 is also required for chondrocyte differentiation through direct activation of Ihh (Wang et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to published literature.

claims.claim: In the E14.5-E17.5 fetal growth plate, ATF4 is expressed in differentiating chondrocytes, with the highest expression in pHCs.
claims.source: In the E14.5-E17.5 fetal growth plate, ATF4 is expressed in differentiating chondrocytes, with the highest expression in pHCs (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: ATF4 expression in HCs progressively decreases after birth and by p10 levels are especially lowered in the LHZ.
claims.source: ATF4 expression in HCs progressively decreases after birth and by p10 levels are especially lowered in the LHZ (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: C10-Atf4 transgenic mice were generated carrying a Col10-Bac-Atf4-IRES-Egfp transgene in which ATF4 expression was driven by the HC-specific promoter of Col10a1.
claims.source: To assess the impact of ATF4 overexpression in HCs in the absence of ER stress, we generated a transgenic mouse model carrying a Col10-Bac-Atf4-IRES-Egfp transgene (hereafter referred to as C10-Atf4) (Figure 2B), in which ATF4 expression was driven by the highly HC-specific promoter of Col10a1 (Leung et al., 2011; Yang et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is a methodological description supported by Figure 2B.

claims.claim: HC-specific expression of the C10-Atf4 transgene was confirmed in developing growth plates from fetal (E15.5) to adult (p20) stages.
claims.source: We confirmed HC-specific expression of the C10-Atf4 transgene in the developing growth plates from fetal (E15.5) to adult (p20) stages (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by expression data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B.

claims.claim: Adult C10-Atf4 transgenic mice were dwarfs, being approximately 20% shorter than wild-type littermates.
claims.source: Similar to 13del mice, adult C10-Atf4 transgenic mice were dwarfs, being approximately 20% shorter than wild-type littermates (Figure 2C and D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by radiographic and body length measurements shown in Figure 2C and D.

claims.claim: Histological analyses revealed growth plate abnormality in both the appendicular and axial skeleton of C10-Atf4 mice.
claims.source: Histological analyses revealed growth plate abnormality in both the appendicular and axial skeleton. These defects are illustrated by the greater than three-fold expansion of the HZ of the tibia and vertebrae of C10-Atf4 mice (Figure 2E; Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by histological data shown in Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and D.

claims.claim: The HZ expansion is more severe in C10-Atf4 mice (threefold of WT) than that in 13del (2.5-fold of WT).
claims.source: Interestingly, the HZ expansion is more severe in C10-Atf4 mice (threefold of WT) than that in 13del (2.5-fold of WT), which is paralleling to the expression level of ATF4.
claims.evidence: This is supported by comparison of histological measurements.

claims.claim: Cell viability was not affected in C10-Atf4 mice.
claims.source: Although forced expression of ATF4 in fibroblasts was reported to decrease survival (Han et al., 2013), cell viability was not affected in C10-Atf4 mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by TUNEL assay data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claims.claim: Overexpression of ATF4 in HCs in the absence of ER stress did not induce transcription of the UPR-associated genes Hspa5 and Ddit3.
claims.source: Importantly, overexpression of ATF4 in HCs in the absence of ER stress did not induce transcription of the UPR-associated genes Hspa5 and Ddit3 (Figure 2F), although Atf3 was slightly upregulated (Han et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is supported by in-situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2F.

claims.claim: Activation of ATF4 alone, in the absence of the ER stress response, is sufficient to alter HC differentiation, disturb endochondral ossification and cause skeletal abnormalities similar to those observed in 13del mice.
claims.source: Therefore, activation of ATF4 alone, in the absence of the ER stress response, is sufficient to alter HC differentiation, disturb endochondral ossification and cause skeletal abnormalities similar to those observed in 13del mice.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the C10-Atf4 mouse phenotype data.

claims.claim: In C10-Atf4 HCs, constitutive ATF4 activation down-regulated the expression of Col10a1 and led to persistent expression of prehypertrophic chondrocyte marker genes Sox9, Col2a1, Ppr and Ihh in the HZ.
claims.source: In C10-Atf4 HCs, constitutive ATF4 activation down-regulated the expression of Col10a1 and led to persistent expression of prehypertrophic chondrocyte marker genes Sox9, Col2a1, Ppr and Ihh in the HZ (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by in-situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: BrdU-labeled HCs were not detectable in the C10-Atf4 HZ after 2 hr.
claims.source: However, BrdU-labeled HCs were not detectable in the C10-Atf4 HZ after 2 hr (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F), suggesting C10-Atf4 HCs did not appear to have progressed through the G1/S checkpoint.
claims.evidence: This is supported by BrdU labeling data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claims.claim: ATF4 ChIP-Seq data showed ATF4 binding peaks in the regulatory regions of Sox9, Sox5, Sox6, Runx2, Gli2 and Gli3.
claims.source: We searched the published ER stress-associated ATF4 ChIP-Seq data (Han et al., 2013) for binding peaks in crucial chondrogenic transcription factor genes, including members of SOX, RUNX, MEF2, GLI and FOXA families. We found ATF4 binding peaks in the regulatory regions of Sox9, Sox5, Sox6, Runx2, Gli2 and Gli3.
claims.evidence: This is supported by analysis of published ChIP-Seq data.

claims.claim: Only the Sox genes were up-regulated in 13del middle and lower zones, but not Gli2 or Gli3.
claims.source: Amongst these, only the Sox genes were up-regulated in 13del middle and lower zones, but not Gli2 or Gli3 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B), suggesting that the Sox family could be the targets of ATF4.
claims.evidence: This is supported by microarray and qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B.

claims.claim: Overexpression of Sox9 in HCs resulted in an expansion of HZ and impaired terminal differentiation of HCs.
claims.source: Notably, overexpression of Sox9 in HCs resulted in an expansion of HZ and impaired terminal differentiation of HCs, similar to the phenotypes observed in C10-Atf4 mice (Hattori et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to published literature.

claims.claim: Two putative C/EBP-ATF4 motifs, named A1 and A2, were identified in the ATF4-binding peak in the Sox9 promoter region.
claims.source: We identified two putative C/EBP-ATF4 motifs, named A1 and A2, in the ATF4-binding peak in the Sox9 promoter region.
claims.evidence: This is based on analysis of the Sox9 promoter sequence.

claims.claim: ATF4 could transactivate luciferase reporters controlled by the Sox9 promoter in transfection assays in ATDC5 chondrocyte cells.
claims.source: By transfection assays in ATDC5 chondrocyte cells, we found ATF4 could transactivate luciferase reporters controlled by the Sox9 promoter (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: Mutation of A1 and A2 respectively reduced or abolished ATF4 activation of the Sox9 reporters.
claims.source: Mutation of A1 and A2 respectively reduced or abolished ATF4 activation of the Sox9 reporters (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: Anti-ATF4 ChIP-PCR assays demonstrated that ATF4 binds directly to the putative motif region on the Sox9 promoter in vivo.
claims.source: Anti-ATF4 ChIP-PCR assays, using nuclear extracts from E15.5 wild-type and C10-Atf4 limbs, demonstrated that ATF4 binds directly to the putative motif region on the Sox9 promoter in vivo (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by ChIP-PCR data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: Conditional inactivation of Sox9 in C10-Atf4 HC markedly reduced the expansion of HZ.
claims.source: We next assessed the contribution of ATF4 activation of Sox9 in reverting HC differentiation by conditionally inactivating Sox9 in C10-Atf4 HC, using HC-specific Col10a1-Cre (Yang et al., 2014) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A). In the absence of Sox9, the expansion of HZ in C10-Atf4 mice was markedly reduced, and there were fewer cells expressing Col2a1 in the HZ (Figure 4A–C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by histological and quantitative data shown in Figure 4A–C.

claims.claim: Conditional inactivation of Sox9 in 13del mice decreased expression of Col2a1 and Ppr in HC, and the HZ expansion was considerably shortened.
claims.source: Moreover, conditional inactivation of Sox9 in 13del mice decreased expression of Col2a1 and Ppr in HC, and the HZ expansion was considerably shortened (Figure 4D–F; Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by histological and quantitative data shown in Figure 4D–F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and C.

claims.claim: Deletion of Sox9 in wild-type HCs did not affect chondrocyte hypertrophy.
claims.source: Deletion of Sox9 in wild-type HCs did not affect chondrocyte hypertrophy (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by histological data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claims.claim: ER stress-induced overexpression of ATF4 reverts differentiation in 13del HC by direct activation of Sox9 in HCs, thereby perturbing chondrocyte hypertrophy.
claims.source: Collectively, these data suggest ER stress-induced overexpression of ATF4 reverts differentiation in 13del HC by direct activation of Sox9 in HCs, thereby perturbing chondrocyte hypertrophy.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the genetic rescue experiments.

claims.claim: CHOP is preferentially expressed in the PERK signaling pathway, downstream of p-eIF2α and ATF4.
claims.source: CHOP is another prominent transcription factor that was active in 13del HCs, revealed by bioinformatics analysis. It is preferentially expressed in the PERK signaling pathway, downstream of p-eIF2α and ATF4, which regulates protein synthesis via the PPP1R15A negative feedback loop and restores protein synthesis and induces oxidative stress via Ero1l (Han et al., 2013; Marciniak et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: Overexpression of CHOP in the bone microenvironment in transgenic mice has been reported to impair osteoblastic function leading to osteopenia.

results.result: The manuscript provides background on the integrated stress response (ISR) and unfolded protein response (UPR), describing their activation by various stresses, the role of eIF2α phosphorylation, preferential translation of ATF4 and CHOP, and the three UPR arms (PERK, IRE1α, ATF6). This background establishes the context for skeletal disorders caused by ER stress.
results.evaluation: These claims (C1, C6-C33) represent established knowledge in the field, supported by multiple citations to published literature. They provide necessary background context for understanding the experimental work and are appropriately referenced.

results.result: Prior work on MCDS mouse models and related skeletal disorders demonstrates that ER stress causes chondrocyte differentiation defects, with the 13del model showing reversed differentiation to a more juvenile state. Previous therapeutic approaches targeting protein degradation showed incomplete rescue.
results.evaluation: These claims (C36-C44) summarize prior published work on MCDS and related disorders, appropriately cited. They establish the rationale for the current study by showing that previous approaches were incomplete, justifying investigation of the ISR pathway.

results.result: Transcriptome analysis of fractionated growth plate chondrocytes from 13del mice identified four gene clusters with distinct expression patterns. Cluster I (453 genes) showed upregulation in 13del HCs and enrichment for ER stress/UPR genes. Clusters II/III showed re-expression of prehypertrophic markers (Sox9, Ppr, Ihh) in 13del, while Cluster IV hypertrophy genes were downregulated.
results.evaluation: The transcriptome analysis (C47-C59) is well-supported by microarray data, k-means clustering, and ontological analyses shown in Figure 1. The fractionation methodology is described and validated with marker genes. Comparison with other MCDS models strengthens the findings.

results.result: The PERK-p-eIF2α pathway dominates the UPR response in 13del HCs, with enrichment of PERK pathway genes and ATF4/CHOP binding motifs in Cluster I genes. The IRE1-Xbp1 pathway plays a minimal role, as Xbp1 inactivation or overexpression did not affect the phenotype.
results.evaluation: Claims C60-C66 are supported by multiple lines of evidence: pathway enrichment analysis, motif analysis, ChIP-seq data analysis, and functional validation with Xbp1 transgenic mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 3). The conclusion that PERK dominates over IRE1 is well-justified.

results.result: ATF4 overexpression in hypertrophic chondrocytes (C10-Atf4 mice) is sufficient to cause skeletal abnormalities similar to 13del mice, including dwarfism and HZ expansion, without inducing ER stress markers. ATF4 expression normally decreases postnatally in HCs.
results.evaluation: The C10-Atf4 transgenic model (C70-C77) provides strong evidence that ATF4 alone is sufficient for the phenotype. The data include radiographs, body measurements, histology (Figure 2), and expression analysis showing no UPR induction. This is a key finding demonstrating ATF4's causal role.

results.result: ATF4 directly transactivates Sox9 by binding to C/EBP-ATF4 motifs in the Sox9 promoter. In C10-Atf4 mice, this leads to persistent expression of prehypertrophic markers (Sox9, Col2a1, Ppr, Ihh) in the HZ and downregulation of Col10a1.
results.evaluation: Claims C78-C86 are supported by multiple complementary approaches: ChIP-seq analysis identifying ATF4 binding sites, luciferase reporter assays showing transactivation, ChIP-PCR confirming in vivo binding (Figure 3), and expression analysis. The molecular mechanism is well-established.

results.result: Conditional deletion of Sox9 in C10-Atf4 and 13del HCs markedly reduced HZ expansion and decreased expression of prehypertrophic markers, demonstrating that ATF4-induced Sox9 expression is responsible for the differentiation defects.
results.evaluation: The genetic rescue experiments (C87-C90) provide strong functional validation shown in Figure 4. The reduction of phenotype severity upon Sox9 deletion in both models, with no effect in wild-type, demonstrates Sox9's essential role downstream of ATF4.

results.result: CHOP plays a pro-survival role in 13del HCs. Ablating CHOP in 13del mice exacerbated skeletal defects, increased HZ expansion, and caused increased apoptosis, despite upregulation of ER stress sensors and chaperones.
results.evaluation: The 13del;Ddit3-/- compound mutant analysis (C95-C99) is well-supported by histology, TUNEL assays, and transcriptome data (Figure 5). The increased apoptosis and worsened phenotype clearly demonstrate CHOP's pro-survival function, contrasting with its typical pro-apoptotic role.

results.result: Fgf21 is the most upregulated gene in 13del HCs and requires both ATF4 and CHOP for induction. ATF4 alone is necessary but not sufficient, as both factors bind to the Fgf21 promoter under ER stress. Fgf21 expression was reduced in 13del;Ddit3-/- mice.
results.evaluation: Claims C100-C108 are supported by microarray data, in situ hybridization, immunoblotting, luciferase assays, and ChIP-PCR (Figure 6). The requirement for both ATF4 and CHOP is demonstrated by the lack of induction in C10-Atf4 mice and reduction in Ddit3-/- mice.

results.result: FGF21 protects 13del HCs from apoptosis in a cell-autonomous and dosage-dependent manner. Chimera experiments showed that Fgf21-expressing cells could not rescue adjacent Fgf21-/- cells, demonstrating cell-autonomous action.
results.evaluation: The Fgf21 genetic analysis and chimera experiments (C109-C115) provide strong evidence for FGF21's cell-autonomous pro-survival role. TUNEL assays, chimera analysis with EGFP marking, and correlation analysis (Figure 7) support the dosage-dependent, cell-autonomous mechanism.

results.result: The PERK pathway dominates in causing dysplasia by reverting chondrocyte differentiation via ATF4-directed transactivation of Sox9. Chondrocyte survival is enabled by CHOP and dual CHOP-ATF4 transactivation of Fgf21. ISRIB treatment prevents differentiation defects and ameliorates chondrodysplasia.
results.evaluation: These abstract claims (C2-C5) summarize the major findings of the manuscript. They are well-supported by the comprehensive experimental evidence including transcriptomics, transgenic models, genetic rescue experiments, and pharmacological intervention described in the detailed results.

results.result: ISRIB, an ISR inhibitor targeting eIF2-eIF2B interaction, ameliorated skeletal deformities in 13del mice when administered from E13.5 to p20 or postnatally. Treatment reduced dwarfism, improved skeletal measurements, and decreased HZ expansion in a dosage-dependent manner without adverse effects in wild-type mice.
results.evaluation: The ISRIB treatment studies (C119-C124) are well-supported by extensive data including body measurements, radiographic analyses, and histology (Figure 8 and supplements). Both prenatal and postnatal treatment protocols were tested with appropriate controls, showing dosage-dependent efficacy.

results.result: ISRIB acts by inhibiting preferential translation of ATF4 without affecting p-eIF2α levels, leading to downregulation of ATF3, DDIT3, and downstream targets including SOX9. The IRE1/Xbp1 pathway was unaffected, confirming selectivity. Importantly, ISRIB did not induce apoptosis despite lowering ATF4, CHOP, and FGF21 levels.
results.evaluation: The mechanism of ISRIB action (C125-C133) is thoroughly characterized by immunostaining, immunoblotting, qRT-PCR, and TUNEL assays (Figure 9). The data show selective inhibition of PERK pathway without affecting Xbp1 or inducing apoptosis, demonstrating therapeutic titration of the pathway.
